purpose: Evolving hypotheses about audible likeness, tested with regular human listening including model/metric agreement cases.

hypotheses.claim: A chosen winner can still fail to evoke the reference.
hypotheses.evidence: The neural-v2 quick export contained four best choices; the user separately said only charm2.wav was actually approximated.
hypotheses.nextTest: Retain best/none choices and invite optional close-enough or failure notes; do not relabel all winners as successful recreations.

observations.finding: The user qualified the two new winners: book-close has the same general character but is still a bit off; charm2 is closeish, approaching a recreation. This adds partial absolute-likeness evidence without establishing fully convincing success or numerical ratings.

The user explicitly reports no convincing recreations across all five pitch-calibration references, despite five best choices. Zero of five is the absolute adequacy outcome; retain the seven pairwise preferences without treating winners as successful reproductions. Improving selection among these presented options cannot alone solve the batch. No particular acoustic cause is established.

Immediate candidate-scoped answers give three preferred new outputs very-close labels, the preferred older Boomr option a similar label, and reject both Footsteppr options. Five of six references submitted; no missing judgment or scalar score is inferred. This finally separates the absolute and relative evidence within the questionnaire.

hypotheses.claim: Models and similarity metrics can agree while sharing an audible blind spot.
hypotheses.evidence: On 2026-10-04 the user requested continued involvement even when models and metrics agree and emphasized developing psychoacoustic theories from listening.
hypotheses.nextTest: Include claimed successes and representative coverage alongside uncertain cases in regular short listening batches.

observations.finding: Human choices disagree with frozen matching distance on bird and one spinout pair; objective agrees with four of six heard-only pairs. This establishes concrete metric disagreement on these cases, not consensus across several independent models or a general error rate.

Both MatchObjective and preference-neural-v2 favor the new option on all five references. They agree with three of four strict heard preferences, but both favor the rejected new Boomr option. The strong numerical Footsteppr improvement is still explicitly not close. Metric agreement is not an adequacy certificate.

New Footsteppr is preferred and very close despite worse matching distance; older Boomr wins the untouched short burst and is very close despite worse matching distance. MatchObjective agrees with 3/5 strict pairs, frozen preference-neural-v2 with 4/5. Metric agreement and lower loss are not adequate stand-ins for listening.

hypotheses.claim: Some pitch-register and gesture errors matter more than aggregate spectral improvements.
hypotheses.evidence: The user reported poor pitch matching. The forward pilot also found lower actual descriptor loss with substantially worse pitch and motion; this is diagnostic evidence, not a listening validation of a new weighting rule.
hypotheses.nextTest: Compare real renders while preserving already matched reliable pitch and motion. Keep noisy targets outside pitch constraints; ask whether retained pitch/gesture produces better likeness.

observations.finding: For bird, the preferred original Bfxr has an estimated median pitch near 2,402 Hz versus target 2,537 Hz; the rejected new Pluckr is near 3,835 Hz despite lower total distance. For charm2, the preferred new Bfxr is near 634 Hz versus target 637 Hz and original Bfxr 1,046 Hz. These observations are consistent with register mattering, but timbre/gesture also differ and pitch estimators have known failures; this is not a causal isolation.

The new gentle rise and wide rising sweep are explicitly very close, but the strict pitch guards would reject them when using their displayed previous candidates as hypothetical baselines. The gentle rise loses one paired voiced frame; the wide sweep has worse measured contour error and an audition-only direction flip. These are proxy failures, not evidence that register or gesture no longer matter.

hypotheses.claim: An input descriptor with an octave error can make wrong-register reproductions appear plausible to the inverse and matching pipeline.
hypotheses.evidence: The bird reference produced roughly 2.54 kHz in the older pitch diagnostic and 1.23 kHz in the coarse neural descriptor. Clean sine probes isolate descriptor errors: 2,000 Hz becomes roughly 1,002 Hz and 3,200 Hz becomes 1,575 Hz. The older diagnostic itself halves a 4,000 Hz sine. None of the new flat/temporal/mixture raw inverses passed a one-semitone check on four additional high-pitch development probes. This does not isolate the input error as the cause of the full model failures.
hypotheses.nextTest: Use the fixed diagnostic to test broader pitch training coverage separately. First ask for human listening on the bounded calibration component; do not infer general likeness from register agreement.

observations.finding: Controlled pitch-only retraining regressed overall on 20 fixed development probes. Strong low fundamentals with weak 20th partials expose a new ACF initial-lobe failure, reproduced on actual Bfxr/Transfxr Whistle rows; clean sine tests were insufficient. High-pitch median-only passes and realized coverage counts are therefore not trusted as fundamental estimates on these timbres. No new listening claims or human labels.

Correcting the initial-lobe diagnostic defect did not improve the trained inverse overall: ordinary mean objective1.435681→1.864569, moving direction6/8→3/8. Retained as a negative result; the input bug was real but did not explain all model failures. Frozen-v3 proposals with bounded actual-render calibration subsequently cleared a predeclared24-probe gate, recovering4/4high registers; this is a hybrid inference result, not a retraining win.

hypotheses.claim: Attack character, event rhythm and tail may explain likeness failures that a pooled spectrum misses.
hypotheses.evidence: User emphasizes large-scale gestural qualities and feel. No causal ablation has established the appropriate balance for this corpus.
hypotheses.nextTest: Use controlled encoder comparisons and optional human failure descriptions; test any inferred rule on different sound families before broad adoption.

observations.finding: The user says the short noisy book-close sound is in the same genre, but the distinction between similar and exact is hard to judge and it remains off. This motivates separating event-family recognition from finer transient/texture fidelity; it does not identify which acoustic component caused the remaining mismatch.

hypotheses.claim: Exact control reconstruction can penalize acoustically equivalent patches, consuming model capacity without improving sound similarity.
hypotheses.evidence: evaluations/transfxr-pitch-identifiability.json records identical non-silent PCM for one fixed Transfxr White setup at nominal 2800, 4000 and 5000 Hz, while a tonal control changes. The frozen Transfxr loss still adds pitch-octave penalties. This does not imply pitch is always irrelevant for noise.
hypotheses.nextTest: After the controlled v5 input experiment, test audibility-aware loss or equivalence handling on separately rendered sensitivity pairs; retain all inputs/data, compare actual sound outputs, and ask for human review even when metrics agree.

hypotheses.claim: Requiring a large fraction of target-active frames to carry matching pitch can replace an already accurate pitch/timbre candidate with a more continuously voiced candidate.
hypotheses.evidence: pitch-calibration-v1/paired/031-Pluckr-static: baseline Pluckr median error0.00566semitone and objective0.422535; target-active pitch coverage0.7045 fails the0.75eligibility rule. Selected Bfxr has coverage1.0 but objective3.076493. Target/baseline/selected voicedframes44/31/47. This demonstrates the selector tradeoff; no human preference has been established.
hypotheses.nextTest: Retain uncalibrated baselines in short listening comparisons. Examine attack/tail and event feel when pitch constraints change the winning engine; do not silently treat voicing coverage as perceptual ground truth.

observations.finding: On the five fixed tagged references, selection changes only Select Beep and heavy impact bell; charm2, battleStart and Descending Fall Whistle fall back unchanged. battleStart has adjusted Transfxr proposals near measured register but only 0.435 target-active pitch coverage, so none qualifies. This is partial diagnostic transfer, not human evidence that the conservative rule is correct. Human comparison pending.

Both calibrated changes lose: uncalibrated Bfxr wins the beep and original Bfxr wins the bell. The unchanged Transfxr whistle wins. Thus the passing synthetic pitch gate fails to establish human improvement; this does not isolate which jointly changed timbre, contour or envelope cue caused rejection.

hypotheses.claim: A single global weighting of pitch, timbre and envelope may not express which cue dominates likeness for each reference.
hypotheses.evidence: The latest preferred beep is worse in 24/30 current distance components, while six spectrum/timbre/correlation components favor it. The preferred bell instead gains on envelope/event cues. Refitting the existing 30-component global scorer gives only 3/7 held-out and 4/7 full-fit agreement on the latest comparisons, despite about 73% held-out reference-balanced agreement overall. These are descriptive correlations, not evidence that conditioning will solve the problem.
hypotheses.nextTest: Keep the current refit experimental. Target-conditioned cue weights remain a possible ranking experiment, but the explicit zero-of-five convincing outcome also requires improved candidate generation. Compare candidate-generation changes against frozen baselines on held-out actual renders and a fresh human listening batch. Ranking agreement alone is not an adequacy gate.

hypotheses.claim: Threshold-based trimming can turn tiny quantization differences into large relative-time pitch diagnostic changes.
hypotheses.evidence: For the human-approved wide rise, normalized float and audition PCM16 have reported directions +1 and -1. Quantization extends the trim endpoint by 2239 samples. Changing one float tail sample to its quantized value reproduces the flip; keeping the original support while quantizing the interior restores +1. The original audition archive matches the intended export.
hypotheses.nextTest: Measure the existing inverse prediction sensitivity separately before attributing its transfer failures to this defect. Any robust support or augmentation experiment must retain frozen baselines, use fresh data/model bindings, and test held-out actual renders and human likeness.

hypotheses.claim: Separate native-trained inverse experts can add audible coverage while older shared experts remain better on some sounds.
hypotheses.evidence: New Footsteppr wins a Footsteppr source and a Whooshr wingbeat; new Boomr wins rocket burst; old Boomr wins native short burst. All four winners explicitly very close. Native footstep is a similar tie; tagged book-close unsubmitted.
hypotheses.nextTest: Retain both generations; compare original Bfxr, the older ensemble, and new specialists on five new tagged files. Do not infer real transfer or a population success rate from selected native positives.

observations.finding: All five actual tagged references judged. New Footsteppr has two relative wins but each is only least-bad. Older Clonkr footstep is similar; two original Bfxr winners are least-bad. Zero very-close judgments. Synthetic successes do not transfer adequately to this batch.

hypotheses.claim: Pitch penalties on noisy transient sounds may override perceptually useful envelope and timbre improvements.
hypotheses.evidence: For the explicitly very-close preferred specialist footstep, envelope, coverage, mel and timbre terms improve, but pitch contributes 1.2568 versus zero for the older option. Removing pitch/voicing terms changes this pair ordering. The separate short-burst preference error has zero pitch penalty on both and is not explained by this hypothesis.
hypotheses.nextTest: On additional noisy real and synthetic sources, compare pitch estimator confidence with explicit listening outcomes. Preserve reliable tonal pitch checks and hold this pair out of any claimed independent validation. Do not globally remove pitch terms.

hypotheses.claim: A control regressor can miss usable preset regions even when an engine can render similar sounds.
hypotheses.evidence: Five tagged references yielded one similar and four least-bad winners. A frozen 64,415-training-preset search plus four bounded refinement starts per target produces ten novel scorer-selected alternatives, all from retrieved starts. All 1,065 retained candidate waveforms replay exactly. Numerical improvement does not yet establish useful teachers or audible recreation.
hypotheses.nextTest: Listen to frozen matching- and preference-selected outputs beside exact historical winners. If useful candidates exist, investigate multimodal/retrieval-conditioned inversion or distillation; if not, improve representation, objective or synth coverage without training on least-bad pseudo-labels.
